properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/15/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in West Bethlehem Township, Washington county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.

Violation ID: 8165819
Permit API: 125-23126
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: West Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/15/2023
Comments: On 11/15/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Cowden 55 well. On 08/23/2023, a routine partial inspection was conducted (IR 3606258).On 08/23/2023, the tank onsite displayed oil which looked as thought it was dripping down the side fro the top. The oil was on a small section of gravel. A smaller section of oil was on another side of the tank. The operator was notified the day of observation. There were no violations issued on 08/23/2023 due to size of area impacted. During inspection on 11/15/2023, for following was observed: The site appeared remediated regarding the oil from the top of the tank; the operator removed the impacted gravel and placed it in a bucket marked with 08/24/2023. The bucket remianed onsite; I recommend that this is removed and disposed of a an approproate waste facility (Photos 1-4). It also looked as thought the operator had wiped the side of the tank off. During the followup, a conductivity test was performed underneath the lower valve on the tank, which displayed iron stained gravel. Conductivity readings within the iron stained gravel, under the valve, yielded elevated results (Photos 5-7).During the initial inspection, a gas odor was noticed near the wellhead and I informed the operator. They informed operation's to inspect. They informed me that the grey apparatus on the well (Photo 8) was part of the landowner's hookup. When the operator followed up, their gas meter did not detect any gas. During the 11/15/23 follow up, the odor was noticed again to which I informed the operator. They followed up the same day and mentioned that the heater on the landowner's setup was functioning properly and may be bleeding; they recommendded a pressure test be performed. I contacted the landowner to inform them of what Diversified (operator) informed me of - they also contacted the landowner. I contacted the landowner about my conversation with the operator and recommended that the setup receives maintenance. The operator informed me that they thought the odor contained mercaptan and may be coming from a Columbia gas line nearby. Below the wellsite is a Williams station that the gas flows to. Regarding the elevated conductivity observed onsite below the valve of the production tank, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b)

Comments: On 4/7/23 at 0915 hrs., I conducted a follow up inspection of Stonehaven Energy Mgt. Co., LLC's Wise Richard 4 well (API 065-25991) in Henderson Twp., Jefferson Co. A Notice of Violation was issued after an inspection conducted on 10/24/22 in which a production fluid release was documented (insp. ID 3444962, enf. 408609). An Administrative Order was issued on 3/27/23.Upon re-inspection of the site, no evidence of soil excavation or remediation was observed. The production fluid tank remains onsite and is filled to capacity. Production fluid was observed on the ground adjacent to the tank within the fenced in area. These observations are contrary to paragraph 1 of the Order, in which the operator is to "...immediately cease and desist discharging and depositing crude oil, brine, and/or other production fluids to the ground..." and is to "...immediately and permanently remove and/or close any tanks, lines, and/or any other items at or near the wells and/or well spill sites that allow such discharges...".Violations from inspection ID 3444962 remain outstanding and are cited again for this inspection.

Comments: The Department was notified by the Operator on 10/22/2025 of a loss of well control. Halliburton was on site and stimulating the 10H, 12H, 14H, 16H and 20H wells. They noticed an abnormal sudden pressure drop of approx. 2500 psi while stimulating stage 61 out of 91 on the 12H. They shut down and noticed a gas / fluid mist coming from the cellar. Lead Cudd personnel mobilizing from Houston Texas expected at 6:30 pm this evening. Currently Operator is containing release to cellar area and pumping fluid to gas buster storage tank on location. Operator will continue monitoring well pressures and venting (9x5) annulus discharges in a safe contained manner until well control can be restored. Based on the findings made during the Department's initial response to the notification, a violation has been cited for ¿¿78a.73(a). It should be noted that, because Coterra provided a self-reported notification, no violation is being cited for ¿¿78a.86 at this time, which states: "In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under ¿¿ 78a.91 - 78a.98 (related to plugging)." As a result of these findings, please provide a written response by 11/30/2025 detailing the root cause or causes that lead to loss of well control and corrective actions that Coterra proposes to implement to prevent similar failures in the future. In addition, although a violation of ¿¿78a.86 has not been cited, the written response should also include information regarding how Coterra intends to comply with this regulation.

Comments: On June 4, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline and Justin Abbott conducted a follow up inspection at Beech Resources Premier Pad. This inspection was to follow up with the reported spill from June 2, 2020 and an inspection completed by DEP staff on June 3, 2020. The inspection on June 3, 2020 reported an area of high conductivity still remaining in the impacted area. Don Stevenson with Beech Resources and Matt Tunsing with Penn E&R were onsite. Conductivity of the excavated area of impact was screened and 1 or 2 small depressions were noticed that had a reading of 1 mS/cm to 2.5 mS/cm. The normal levels of conductivity were noted outside and downgrade of the previously delineated area of impact. So the area of impact had not changed from previous delineation. Another area was of high conductivity was noted from the inspection on June 3, 2020. That area was at the edge of the permitted MASS onsite where some off loading had taken place. That area had a small puddle of water about 3 ft. long by 2 ft. wide that was screened for conductivity. The conductivity of the water was about 7 mS/cm and the soil around the puddle was 5 mS/cm. Judging from the area that was screened for conductivity the spill appeared to be less than 5 gallons. Beech Resources said that they would collect the water from the puddle and scrape up the impact soil in that area. No new violations noted. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 and Inspection No. 30309142 still remain.

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/29/2024
Comments: On January 29, 2024, inspection conducted at the Fatur Well Pad in Salem Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow-up to IR 3700597, which was conducted by DEP WQS at OGI request. During this inspection, a pink oily substance with elevated conductivity was discovered on the ground next to the onsite GPU unit and within its secondary containment. Violations were issued as a result. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 2 and 3). The compressor noted in IR 3700597 had rags remaining within its secondary containment, soaking up what appears to be a petroleum based substance (see photos 4 and 6). However, it is on the verge of overflowing (see photo 7). No elevated conductivity readings were gathered from this substance (see photo 8), and there did not appear to be any staining on the ground around it. The well head onsite (well 10H) was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). Pooling was observed on the ground around the well head, however this appeared to be snowmelt due to the low conductivity and lack of discoloration (see photo 15). A Hugill's dumpster was observed on the eastern side of the pad dripping a dark fluid onto the ground (see photo 16). Although this fluid was not elevated in conductivity, the DEP recommends that this is addressed by the operator and necessary remediations are conducted if this is a regulated substance. The pink oily fluid observed during the time of IR 3700597 remains in the GPU secondary containment. The conductivity of this substance read 15,990 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 18). The disconnected hose and pink tinted substance remains on the gravel behind the GPU unit. The conductivity of this substance and/or ground surface read 724 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 19). The gear lubricant container holding a substance of similar coloration remains adjacent to the GPU unit (see photo 20). What appears to be a pump attached to the GPU unit was observed to be completely frosted over at the time of inspection (see photo 21). What appears to be an additional pump in disuse was observed on the ground adjacent to the GPU unit. A background soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the woods adjacent to the eastern side of the pad, which read 155.5 Microsiemens. Of the five additional tanks and equipment placed in secondary containment onsite that were not previously noted (see photos 3, 9, 11, 12, and 22), three of them appeared to be holding rainwater at the time of inspection. Violations were issued as a result. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). No elevated conductivity readings were gathered from this substance (see photo 8), and there did not appear to be any staining on the ground around it. The well head onsite (well 10H) was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). Pooling was observed on the ground around the well head, however this appeared to be snowmelt due to the low conductivity and lack of discoloration (see photo 15). Violation ID: 8177498
Permit API: 053-31042
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/28/2024
Comments: This follow up inspection was conducted to evaluate the open violations at this site which were issued on November 21, 2023. The access road and site location have not been stoned. The culverts, ditches, and sumps at this location have been installed. The areas of earth disturbance along the banks of the site and access road have been mulched, however, several areas are not sufficient due to washing away over time. These areas will require added temporary stabilization. Upon arriving at the site at approximately 13:15, there was no precipitation occurring. At approximately 13:30, it began to lightly rain. It was noted that the access roads leading to the proposed wells upslope of the Hastings SDT 47 proposed well site showed evidence of accelerated erosion (see Photos 1 and 2). Due to the up slope road surface not having stone, that the up slope ditches, culverts, and sumps became overwhelmed with sediment laden water (see Photo 3). The culvert at the Hastings SDT 47 site location was receiving a large volume of sediment laden water from the up slope roads (see Photo 4). This sediment laden water was traveling through the woods and directly discharging into Hastings Run (see Photos 5 and 6). Down stream of the discharge, the sediment laden water is clearly pictured from bank to bank (see Photo 7). This photo was taken after the rain had stopped at approximately 14:00. The rain was varying in intensity over the course of the 30 minutes with approximately 10 minutes of heavy down fall. A voicemail was left with the operator, Steven Tachoir, to discuss the results from this inspection. It was recommend to stone the access roads and site location as quickly as possible as weather permits. The issued violations noted from November 21, 2023 will be noted as outstanding as a result of this inspection.

Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: On January 25 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Fatur Well Pad after a Department OGI requested a follow up in regards to a pink oily substance observed on the pad.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The ERP and PPC plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible leaks. Upon inspection of the GPU, there appeared to be a red tinted fluid in the containment surrounding the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and revealed elevated readings of 4.39mS. Upon further inspection, there appeared to be a disconnected hose and red tinted fluid on the gravel behind the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken from the surface on the ground beneath the puddles on the well pad and indicated elevated readings of 1.08mS and 1.37mS in comparison to the background reading of 0.12 mS taken from the surface of the soil along the well site perimeter. Directly adjacent to the GPU was a container with red colored fluid labeled as gear lubricant. The Department recommends the operator assess the red tinted fluid observed on the ground near the GPU as well as inside of the containment and remediate any spills in accordance with Department standards. The Department requests clarification on what the red tinted fluid observed on the ground is and how much was released with in 10 days of receiving this report.Upon inspecting the additional production equipment onsite, there appeared to be oil based matter being absorbed by cloths beneath the compressor. There did not appear to be any staining on the ground surrounding the compressor. The Department recommends the operator ensure the structural integrity of the all production equipment is sound and properly contain and dispose of any production related fluid in the proper manner to prevent any future pollution events. Upon inspection of the area mentioned by an OGI to have a pink oily matter on the ground, it appeared that a majority of the substance may have been washed away by recent rain as only small spots of a pink colored matter was observed on the ground surrounding a production tank next to the compressor. Conductivity readings were taken on the ground where the pink substance was observed and did not indicate elevated reading with readings of 0.13mS and 0.11mS. Upon inspection of the production tank and containment, the pink oily fluid was observed. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and did not indicate elevated readings with a reading of 0.09mS. The Department requests information regarding what was released and how much was released in this area with in 10 days of receipt of this report. The Department recommends removing excess fluids from secondary containments in order to ensure they meet required holding capacities of 110% according to Chapter 78a64a.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the release observed near the GPU, failure to have the gear lubricant in proper secondary containment, and the secondary containment for the production tank near the compressor failing to meet proper storage capacity. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator response.

Comments: Melissa Breitenbach (XTO) called the Department on 02/19/2026 to report a release at the well site which occurred at approximately 3:30 PM that day during plugging. I visited the site on 02/20/2026 and met with George Winebark (Operations Supervisor) to gather additional information.Per Mr. Winebark, the release was the result of a valve failure during the circulation stage, which caused an estimated 10 barrels worth of fluid to be expelled. At the time a water truck was on site and managed to collect most of the water as it was being released, which prevented much of it from reaching the ground or spreading off of the pad. The affected area was approximately 15' long and concentrated along a narrow strip where the water flowed. In the attached photographs, the pink flags show the extent of the release per conductivity readings. The highest conductivity readings (> 3.0 mS/cm) were close to the plugging location, and Mr. Winebark attributes these to historical usage (a since-removed production tank) rather than the released fluid, which was largely freshwater. Off pad, readings peaked at 1.8 mS/cm and dropped to 0.035 mS/cm and below within a foot or two. The release does not appear to have traveled more than 5' off pad. There is a stream approximately 500' downslope of the well pad.A section of what appears to be silt fencing seemed to be overwhelmed near the area where the release flowed off pad. The Department recommends repairing or replacing the fencing to prevent future runoff from continuing downslope. Per Ms. Breitenbach, a consultant has been enlisted to assist with Act 2 clean-up, and plugging will continue through the following week. Reclamation and clean-up will begin following the completion of plugging.

Comments: Melissa Breitenbach (XTO) called the Department on 02/19/2026 to report a release at the well site which occurred at approximately 3:30 PM that day during plugging. I visited the site on 02/20/2026 and met with George Winebark (Operations Supervisor) to gather additional information.Per Mr. Winebark, the release was the result of a valve failure during the circulation stage, which caused an estimated 10 barrels worth of fluid to be expelled. At the time a water truck was on site and managed to collect most of the water as it was being released, which prevented much of it from reaching the ground or spreading off of the pad. The affected area was approximately 15' long and concentrated along a narrow strip where the water flowed. In the attached photographs, the pink flags show the extent of the release per conductivity readings. The highest conductivity readings (> 3.0 mS/cm) were close to the plugging location, and Mr. Winebark attributes these to historical usage (a since-removed production tank) rather than the released fluid, which was largely freshwater. Off pad, readings peaked at 1.8 mS/cm and dropped to 0.035 mS/cm and below within a foot or two. The release does not appear to have traveled more than 5' off pad. There is a stream approximately 500' downslope of the well pad.A section of what appears to be silt fencing seemed to be overwhelmed near the area where the release flowed off pad. The Department recommends repairing or replacing the fencing to prevent future runoff from continuing downslope. Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Comments: On July 26th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a release that occurred at the Porter Well Pad in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The Department was accompanied by Justin Creighan (Olypmus), Bradley Latimer (Olympus) and Shelby (Olympus). On July 26th, 2022, at 6:56AM, the Department was notified by Operator of a release that occurred at 5:00AM earlier that morning at the 12M GPU on the Porter Well Pad. It was reported that approximately over 5 gallons of Glycol was released onto the pad. No impacts to local waterways reported. July 26th, 2022, the Departed contacted Operator for further information regarding release that occurred. Per Operator, around 5:00AM this morning, burner on the 12M GPU did not shut off and caused glycol within containment to release out of filler tube onto the ground and secondary containment. It is estimated that 30-33 gallons was released total. A clam shell was present onsite and crews excavated impacted area and deposited material into drums onsite. SDS sheets for Glycol are onsite and will be made available. On July 26th, 2022, at 1:15PM, the Department conducted an onsite inspection of the Porter Well Pad. At time of inspection, Act 9 Sign was installed at access road entrance (photo 1). ERP and PPC plans were present on site in mailbox. SDS sheets for Glycol were located on site and made available. Impacted area adjacent to 12M GPU appears to be visually remediated. Drums of impacted material were observed onsite within secondary containment. Release quantity determination was explained by Mr. Latimer onsite. Holding capacity for Glycol is 200 gallons, tube height is 6ft, and missing quantity is 1 ft (33.3 gallons). Mr. Latimer confirmed that quantity released was total amount released (within containment and released onto well pad). He also clarified that the thermostat that controls the burner to the GPU malfunctioned by not turning off burner to the GPU and overheating, creating the release of Glycol. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. Violations are being cited as immediately corrected/abated.

Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site.

Inspection Date: 8/06/2024
Comments: On August 6 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well in Dunbar Township, Fayette County. At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the affected area of the pump jack fluid release documented in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. There were erosion and sedimentation issues at the well site and adjacent to the wellhead due to the prior releases of the fluid from the pump jack onto the ground in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. It appears the erosion that previously extended adjacent to and downslope from the well site is now exhibiting greater than 70% vegetative coverage with the exception of the area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead. A background soil conductivity reading was taken. The soil conductivity reading was 0.0370mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the wellhead. The soil conductivity readings were 0.883mS, 0.273mS, 0.407mS, and 0.464mS. Although soil conductivity readings around the wellhead with visually stained gravel were lower compared to previous inspections, these readings are still higher than the background soil conductivity reading. It appears visually that the area around the wellhead and area extending approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead are not remediated due to the stained gravel, the lack of vegetation, and high conductivity readings.The area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead had soil conductivity readings of 4.71mS and 5.46mS. Soil conductivity readings collected by the Department today in the adjacent agricultural field that were affected in previous inspection report 3578365 dated June 22 2023 were 0.0192mS, 0.0698mS, 0.1385mS, 0.1185mS, 0.1918mS, and 0.1324mS.The Department has yet to receive the requested information from the June 22 2023 inspection, September 6th 2023 inspection, and March 1st 2024 inspection. The Department again requests the following information for both spills; evaluate the release that has occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred, to be provided in the requested NOV response by August 9, 2024. The Department also requests waste manifests upon proper disposal of wastes generated from the spill remediation.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.Soil conductivity calibration was conducted on August 6 2024 at 14:22.

Code §§ 78a.54, 78a.56—78a.58 and 78a.60—78a.61.
Violation ID: 972777

Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Comments: 08/09/2023This administrative inspection is being conducted for the Ironman Well Site following violations issued on 07/18/2023 (IR: 3589336, Enf: 418538).Violations of 78a57(a), 78a66(b)1ii, 78a66(b)1i, 78a66(b)2, 91.33(A), 91.34(A), 78a54, and SWMA 301 were issued on 07/18/2023, following an incident inspection conducted in response to a spill report recieved by the Department on 07/17/2023. On 08/02/2023, the Department recieved the 15 Day Report. The following is required to be included within the 15 day report, however deficiencies were noted within, specifically A, D, E, and G: 78a.66. Reporting and remediating spills and releases. (c)(2)(i) Within 15 business days of the spill or release, the operator or other responsible party shall provide an initial written report that includes, to the extent that the information is available, the following:(A) The regulated substance involved.(B) The location where the spill or release occurred.(C) The environmental media affected.(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities.(F) Interim remedial actions planned, initiated or completed.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible partyintends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedulefor site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated timeframes within which it expects to take those actions.The following deficiencies were noted within the 15 Day Report submitted on 08/02/2023:(A) The regulated substance involved: EQT's report mentions leak from dump line, but does not specifically mention the regulated substance.(C) EQT's report did not mention an assessment of potential impact to Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible party intends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedule for site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated time frames within which it expects to take those actions: EQT mentions entering Act 2, but provides no timeline. EQT indicates assessment will focus on dump line trench and northern pad slope, but does not discuss WOC.Due to the deficiencies noted within the 15 Day Report, a violation of 78a66(c)2i is being issued for the failure to provide a complete initial written report within 15 days. Violations issued on 07/18/2023 remain outstanding.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after a truck roll over caused produced fluid to be released along the access road on August 30, 2023. In an email sent to the Department by EQT representative Rick Hall on 9/5/23, he relayed that excavation was complete on the area impacted by the release along the access road. He said that the area of the impact had been delineated by environmental consultant Penn E and R using field instrumentation. He also stated that impacted material which had been excavated was staged within secondary containment on Pad A. Trees have been cleared from the area of the truck rollover on the west side of the access road as well as the area east of the NFG pipeline right-of-way at the north stormwater culvert. The full excavated area has been temporarily stabilized. No fluid was observed in the excavated area. Compost filter sock has been installed as appropriate around the excavated area. No E and S issues noted.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel was 1800 uS/cm. On Pad A, excavated material is tarped and sits within secondary containment. Six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment and they appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release from the MASS on 12/19/22.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/24/2022
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 973250
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/24/2022
Comments: On October 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. DEP spoke with Profrac Company Man Mike Reel and he said they were fracking the 1005H well at the time of inspection. The DEP observed multiple areas of staining adjacent to the containment for the fracking rig. The areas were screened for conductivity with a soil conductivity meter and two areas resulted in over range conductivity readings. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4.0 mS/cm. The first area is adjacent to the frack pumps off the east side of containment. This area of high conductivity is about 12' x 20'. The second area is adjacent to 1 frac tank and 2 gas buster tanks. This area of high conductivity is about 10'x10'. Soil sample 0651-139 was collected from the 10'x10' area. The volume of this spill is unknown because it is uncertain how much was spilled under the frack rig containment. The DEP pointed out the previously mentioned areas to Mr. Reel and he said he would have someone begin scraping up the areas immediately. DEP then placed a phone call to STL Resources Seth Rodriguez to inform him of the findings from the inspection. The DEP recommends assessing the area of elevated conductivity and updating DEP of the findings. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, the DEP recommends pursuing an Act 2 remediation. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in either of the stormwater vaults. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.2 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 3 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 31.7 uS/cm. Seep 4 was not screened due to the current condition of the seep screening area. This area is being driven through by ATVs checking on the freshwater waterline for the Sturgis South stimulation. The area is constantly being driven through to refuel the pumps on the waterline. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 24.7 uS/cm. The infiltration berms 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 11 along the access road are well vegetated and appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berms 1, 4, 6, 7, and 9 along the access road are vegetated but, the areas that are holding water have little vegetation and do not appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 1 off the northwest corner of the pad appears to be holding water and not functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 2 off the northwest corner of the pad and the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the pad are lacking vegetation in the infiltration area. The DEP recommends working on the infiltration berms that are not functioning correctly and reseeding the infiltration berms that are lacking vegetation to prevent an erosion event. The areas of staining along with the elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment on the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 902031
Permit API: 125-28620
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Robinson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/10/2020
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/10/2020 at approximately 2:15 PM. The operator reported that an open top buster tank overflowed during flow back operations and approximately 20 gallons impacted the ground behind the tank. The operator reported a total of approximately 188 gallons total was spilled, with 168 gallons spilling to secondary containment. The operator is reporting that the spill will be remediated in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). Nate Smiell and Brandon Carson with Range are on site, on my arrival. The following is observed: The site is currently in flowback operations (Photo 1). The pad drain has been closed. According to Mr. Smiell, he identified the spill at approximately 12:15 PM on 12/10/2020 during a routine inspection of the site. A time for the incident could not be provided at the time of this inspection. Mr. Smiell stated that it could have occurred anywhere between 12 and 24 hours prior to it being found. According to Mr. Smiell the open top tanks are to be inspected and the contents measured every hour. The Department requests these inspection logs be provided for the 24 hours preceding when it was found. Additionally, the Department requests the secondary containment logs for the past month, and at what time was the secondary containment remediated with the vacuum truck? Mr. Carson stated that it was possible that on-site cameras may have recorded the incident. The Department requests more information on this, whether they were able to record the incident and at what time the incident occurred if it was recorded. SPSI is on site and prepping to begin remediation of the site impacted by the spill. The Department requests photographs of the site post clean up as well as the waste manifest once it becomes available. The Department recommended to Mr. Smiell that the operator increase the length of the secondary containment (Photo 2 & 6). Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, more violations may be forthcoming.

Permit API: 051-24284
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 7/10/2026
Comments: On 7/10/26 at 12:50 p.m. Oil and Gas Inspector John Shaffer performed a follow up inspection of the SWIANTEK 1 OG well. Permit number# 051-24284. At the time of the inspection an Act 9 sign was present, but the operator information present is for Big Dog Energy. The well is operated by Diversified Prod LLC and has not been transferred. A violation of 78a.55i(4)(ii) has occurred. The Emergency Response Plan was not found onsite. A violation of 78a.55(i)5vi has occurred. A well label (tag) is attached to the well. The tag includes Big Dog Energy's name and emergency contact information. While the tag contains the permit number and satisfies 3211(h), the tag should be updated to remove the incorrect operator information. A posting containing Diversified Production LLC's information is present. Well appears to be shut in at the visible valves. There are two production units onsite. Production unit one appears to be connected, however production unit 2 is not, which is a violation of OGA3216(C). The Annual Production Reports for production years 2024, 2025, and 2026 have been submitted. They have been submitted with zero or no values and the comments "Sold this well", and "Sold to Big Dog Energy 10/2023". The Mechanical Integrity Assessments have been submitted for production years 2025 without the required information under 78a.88(b)1-4. Under the Standard Comments for No Inspection column it states "This is not our well". This well is included on Order 445705 and will be address consistent with the requirements of the order. Violation 78a55(i)4ii is being added at this time for displaying the incorrect Operators company information on the Act 9 sign. Violation 78a55(i)5vi is being added at this time for not having an Emergency Response Plan onsite. Violation 78.88(b)1-4 is being added at this time as Mechanical Integrity Assessments have been submitted without the required information. Violation OGA3216(C) is being continued in this inspection for not removing equipment onsite not needed for production.
